comparison.objective: Reassemble a table fan by keying the blade, tightening a left-hand spinner while holding the blade, and clipping the grille; the candidate adjusts and locks a gripper stop.
comparison.physical_skill: Both include counterholding against tightening reaction, but PR-2189 stabilizes a freely rotating blade while fastening a separate spinner and assembling clips; the candidate preserves an adjustable screw position while its concentric jam nut is tightened.
comparison.success_condition: PR-2189 requires blade-pin engagement, a tight spinner, four closed grille clips, and release; the candidate requires a 90° stop, retained nuts, three repeatable cycles, bounded drift, and clearance.
comparison.reason: The shared counterholding primitive is generic; maintaining a calibrated screw setting under jam-nut reaction and validating stop repeatability is a different core ability from multipart fan assembly.
